name: Cost-driven nonadherence — fix the barrier, not the patient
label: Synthetic regression eval case — hand-labeled. Not clinical validation.
description: Patient stopped a brand-name ARB because of cost and BP has drifted up. The correct plan addresses the cost barrier (generic/formulary switch, 90-day fills) rather than intensifying, lecturing, or restarting the unaffordable drug.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: Your pressure is up today — one forty-nine over ninety-three. It was well controlled in the spring. Are you still taking the olmesartan?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I have to be honest — I stopped about six weeks ago. My insurance changed and it went to ninety dollars a month. I can't do that.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: I'm glad you told me, and that's a completely fixable problem. Did it work well for you otherwise? Any side effects?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It worked great and I felt fine on it. It's just the price.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: There are very similar medicines that cost a few dollars a month as generics. Let's switch you to one of those today.

expected_information_gaps: which equivalent generic is on the patient's current formulary
medication status conflict: EHR active vs patient stopped — needs reconciliation
forbidden_unsupported_actions: restart brand olmesartan while ignoring the stated cost barrier
add a second antihypertensive on top of the stopped one
frame the plan as a compliance lecture without addressing cost

expected_escalation_or_wait.detail: Act today: switch to an affordable generic in the same class (clinician decision), consider 90-day fills, and recheck BP and potassium in 2-4 weeks. Waiting is wrong; escalation is also wrong.

hand_label_notes: Barrier-matching case. Expected: medication (generic same-class substitution + refill logistics), follow_up (2-4 week recheck; potassium at that visit is acceptable given prior tolerance and normal recent values). A 'lab now before any decision' action is not required here — distinguish from case_01 where labs are stale AND kidney function is borderline.
